state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. Every `Core\Ldap` class owes nothing except `Core\Ldap\Connection`, whose `modify` and `delete` owe everything, tests included. `Core\Ldap\Entry::isDeleted` and `Core\Ldap\Connection::rename` have all their files. Their benches still need `bun nv proofs --record-perf` after a green `bun nv verify`, if this session did not get to it.

**Two blocks reach `samba-ad`.** `[ldap.corp]` binds as the read-only `Reader` and is granted by directory to every `Ldap-*` tree. `[ldap.corp-accounts]` binds as `Administrator` and is granted only to the `setPassword`, `changePassword`, `rename` and `isDeleted` directories and bench files, by a nested `[[app]] root` or `entry` in the root `nvs.toml`. A program that writes adds its own unit outside `OU=Company`, with its own `sAMAccountName`, and deletes both again (playbook § *Writing a test case*). An `[[app]] root` that names a missing directory fails every program with `E0605`, so create the example, the attack and the bench before the first run. Check a draft with `bun nv proofs --run --id '<feature>' --show`, which takes **one** `--id`; `--bless` takes files.

**`bun nv verify` is red at `conformance` with nothing failed.** Every case passes (2753 passed, 0 failed), but the store keeps 89 `lang/` and `reject/` cases red with no keys, from `interpolation-reaches-an-array-offset.nvst` on; `bun nv select --json` lists them. Running that batch by hand with `nvs test --cases <list> --record <dir>` passes and writes 178 recordings, so the cause is in `tools/nv/select/record.ts` `recordCases` and not yet found.

**Seeded facts a proof can print:** people are `CN=Anna Berg`, `CN=Ben Kohl`, `CN=Carla Diaz` and `CN=Dora Lind` under `OU=Company`, plus `CN=Reader`. A deleted entry keeps its `objectSid`, and `Filter::equals('objectSid', $sid->toString())` finds it with `showDeleted: true`; a search by name also finds the deleted entries of earlier runs. As `Administrator`, a `modify` of a deleted entry succeeds. A `rename` of one entry takes about 40 ms on Samba, so a loop of them stays in the hundreds.

**The Rust tests for writes** are in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs`: `a_write_to_a_global_catalog_block_throws_before_it_is_sent` calls `modify` and `delete` without a `covers:` marker, and `unit()` builds an OU's attributes.
